analysis:
The only change in this PR is a documentation addition to docs/reference/configuration.md (head line 414): a new row for `DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SHAPE_WARMUP`, an environment control for load-time shape warmup of ordinary `EngineV2` slots. It adds no executable code. The row says that disabling values are `0`/`false`/`no`/`off` and that `always` skips the probe. It says the warmup is probe-gated, with a 128-token shader-cache probe run twice, and bounded to 20 seconds per engine. It also says the warmup trains no rate or counter and that the variable is forwarded to the LaunchAgent.

I checked the row against the threat-model assets and boundaries, mainly TB-007 and T-029/T-010 (availability), A-001 and T-028/T-041 (prompt and KV residue). The row is consistent with them. Warmup runs at load time, before any consumer data. It is described as excluded from counters and rate training, which suggests no consumer plaintext is used and no routing or telemetry evidence is poisoned. It adds no new network, key, attestation or authorization surface. The LaunchAgent forwarding is an operator-controlled local environment variable, so it falls inside the existing operator trust (TB-003) and is not a new privilege path.

I saw only the documentation. The implementation in `ModelCalibrationPolicy.swift` and the claim that warmup uses synthetic inputs, honors the 20-second bound and does not touch the prefix cache or SSD tier are outside the supplied evidence and unverified. If code changes accompany this doc, the next pass should check three things. First, that warmup uses synthetic tokens and does not donate to or read from the SSD prefix cache (T-041). Second, that the time bound holds so it cannot extend startup availability (T-029, T-057). Third, that the LaunchAgent passthrough allow-list change does not forward unvalidated values. The rest of the file is unchanged context and I raised nothing about it.
